entries.topic: Faces, drones and satellites: Clearview, Mobile Fortify, CBP biometrics, NIST, wrongful arrests, Anduril towers, CBP drones, Starshield, SBI awards, Rekognition moratorium

claims.text: Mobile Fortify (404 Media, 17 Jul 2025): ICE app lets an officer point a phone at a face and compare it against ~200 million images, returning name, DOB, nationality, alien number and removal-order status; draws on DHS, State, CBP, FBI and state records

DHS Privacy Threshold Analysis (Feb 2025, via 404 Media FOIA; Reason 3 Nov 2025): 'ICE does not provide the opportunity for individuals to decline or consent'; photos retained 15 years incl. US citizens; checks against CBP Traveler Verification Service; Rep. Thompson said ICE indicated it would prioritise a match over a birth certificate

CBP final rule (published Nov 2025, effective 26 Dec 2025) lets CBP photograph all noncitizens at entry and exit at air, land and sea; noncitizen photos may be kept up to 75 years; US citizens' verification photos deleted within 12 hours and citizens may opt out

7th Cir. (No. 25-1673, 13 Jul 2026) vacated approval of Clearview BIPA class settlement (23% equity stake) because the nationwide class lacked separate representation; remanded; Clearview scrapes public web photos and builds 'facial vectors'
ICE finalised a Clearview contract on 5 Sep 2025: $9.2m ceiling, $3.75m obligated, sole-source citing 'unique proprietary capabilities', for child exploitation and assault-on-officer investigations

NIST (19 Dec 2019): 189 algorithms from 99 developers; majority show demographic differentials; 1:1 false positives for Asian and African American faces often 10 to 100 times higher; most equitable also among most accurate
Washington Post (Jan 2025, via Fortune): at least 8 people wrongfully arrested after facial recognition, 7 Black; 15 departments in 12 states; alibis not checked in 6
Anduril announced (Jun 2026) a $363m CBP award for more than 200 Extended Range Sentry Towers, detecting and tracking objects beyond 5 miles, integrated with its Lattice software

Reuters (Mar 2024): SpaceX's Starshield building hundreds of spy satellites for the NRO under a $1.8bn contract signed 2021; ~a dozen prototypes since 2020; near-continuous imagery; network separate from Starlink; NRO declined to detail SpaceX role
404 Media (23 Sep 2025) from FOIA flight logs: CBP flew drones at least 50 times in support of ICE, Mar 2024-Mar 2025; CBP said Predator flights over LA protests were 'officer safety surveillance'
Space Force space-based interceptor OTAs: 12 firms incl. SpaceX and Anduril, $3.2bn combined ceiling, demo 2028; Palantir not listed
Amazon announced a one-year moratorium on police use of Rekognition on 10-11 Jun 2020; IBM ended its facial recognition program

entries.topic: Code and cloud: GitHub-ICE, takedowns, ICEBlock and court ruling, JWCC, C2E, Oracle-Palantir, FedRAMP 20x

claims.text: GitHub renewed a ~$200,000 ICE licence (Nov 2019) despite staff protest; CEO Nat Friedman said the company 'can't be held responsible' for customer use; $500,000 donated to immigration nonprofits; at least five employees quit
GitHub transparency (29 Sep 2026): 98 government takedown requests in 2025, 708 in H1 2026, mostly a counting change (duplicates and all request types), not more removals

Apple removed ICEBlock and similar apps on 2-3 Oct 2025 after DOJ request; Bondi: 'ICEBlock is designed to put ICE agents at risk just for doing their jobs'; Apple cited law-enforcement information on safety risks
Joshua Aaron sued Bondi, Noem, Lyons and Homan in D.C. federal court on 8 Dec 2025 alleging First Amendment violations; >1 million users at removal

Judge Jorge Alonso (N.D. Ill., ~17 Apr 2026, Rosado case brought by FIRE for an 'ICE Sightings - Chicagoland' Facebook group and the 'Eyes Up' app) found injuries 'likely traceable to government-coerced enforcement' and preliminarily enjoined DOJ/DHS from pressuring Apple and Facebook
JWCC: $9bn ceiling, AWS, Google, Microsoft, Oracle, 7 Dec 2022, all classification levels; JEDI single-vendor $10bn cancelled
CIA C2E (Nov 2020): AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM; 'tens of billions'; ~15 years; CIA plus 16 IC agencies; AWS had served CIA since 2013

Oracle-Palantir (Apr 2024): Foundry workloads to OCI and Gotham/AIP deployable across Oracle's distributed cloud incl. air-gapped regions for defence and intelligence; 'up to the customer which cloud to deploy on'
FedRAMP 20x announced Mar 2025: automated Key Security Indicators; Phase 1 authorisations without agency sponsor; Phase 3 active; High pilot FY27

entries.topic: AI layer: EO 14148, July 2025 orders, CDAO awards, Grok for Government, OneGov, GenAI.mil, Palantir-Anthropic-AWS, Anthropic supply-chain-risk case, OpenAI classified deal

claims.text: EO 14148 (20 Jan 2025) §2(ggg) revoked EO 14110 of 30 Oct 2023 (the Biden AI order); §2(q) revoked EO 14006

23 Jul 2025: three orders signed incl. 'Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government' (procure 'truth-seeking', ideologically neutral models), a deregulation order and an AI exports order, alongside the AI Action Plan
CDAO (14 Jul 2025): awards up to $200M each to Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and xAI for 'agentic AI workflows'
xAI launched 'Grok for Government' on 14 Jul 2025, days after apologising for Grok's antisemitic posts

GSA OneGov (25 Sep 2025): Grok 4 for 42 cents per agency, to Mar 2027; OpenAI and Anthropic $1 per agency per year; earlier xAI deal fell through after antisemitic output (Wired); 30+ groups objected; GSA said Grok 4 met its guidelines
GenAI.mil: Gemini for Government first (Dec 2025 rollout plan, >3m personnel); ChatGPT and Grok (via Starshield AI) added 31 Aug 2026 at IL5; Claude not on it after the dispute
7 Nov 2024: Claude on Palantir AIP hosted on AWS at IL6 (Secret); Anthropic said AUP exceptions are 'carefully calibrated' for 'carefully selected government agencies'

26 Feb 2026: Amodei said Anthropic 'cannot in good conscience accede' and named mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons; Pentagon (Parnell) said it has no interest in illegal mass surveillance and asked use 'for all lawful purposes', 'We will not let ANY company dictate the terms'

Ultimatum 24 Feb 2026; Hegseth announced supply-chain-risk direction 27 Feb; formal 3 Mar; Emil Michael: 'no private company will insert their opinions in the chain of command'; D.C. Cir. 25 Sep 2026 (Katsas, Rao; Henderson dissenting) ruled for the Pentagon; Anthropic 'respectfully disagree[s]'
D.C. Cir. upheld the 41 USC 4713 (FASCSA) designation, 'bad motive' not required; N.D. Cal. on 27 Aug 2026 set aside the 10 USC 3252 designation (adversary requirement) under a permanent injunction
As of 21 Oct 2026: en banc rehearing sought; 17 former national-security officials filed a brief supporting rehearing; no ruling yet

27-28 Feb 2026: Trump ordered agencies to stop using Anthropic; OpenAI agreed to deploy models on a classified network, cloud-only; Altman said the agreement includes 'prohibitions on domestic mass surveillance' and 'human responsibility for the use of force'

entries.topic: Money rails: BSA filings, Choke Point, EO 14331, OCC findings, EO 14178, GENIUS Act text, stablecoin freezes

claims.text: FinCEN FY2024: 4.7 million SARs (~12,870 a day) and 20.5 million CTRs; DHS personnel ran about 290,000 BSA-related queries

Operation Choke Point began 2013; FDIC high-risk list incl. payday lenders and firearms/ammunition sellers, rescinded 2015; DOJ letter 16 Aug 2017: 'no longer in effect, and it will not be undertaken again'

EO 14331 (7 Aug 2025): defines politicized or unlawful debanking (political or religious beliefs, or lawful business disfavoured for political reasons); regulators to remove reputation risk within 180 days; SBA 60 days, reinstatement 120; AG referral only for religion-based debanking (§5(c))

OCC Dec 2025 preliminary findings, nine largest banks: 2020-23 restrictions on sectors incl. firearms, private prisons, coal, Arctic oil, payday lending, tobacco, adult entertainment, PACs and political parties, digital assets, often reputational; ~100,000 complaints under review; no political/religious finding yet
EO 14178 (23 Jan 2025) §5(a): agencies 'prohibited from undertaking any action to establish, issue, or promote CBDCs' unless required by law; revoked EO 14067

GENIUS Act text: issuer 'shall be treated as a financial institution for purposes of the Bank Secrecy Act' (§4(a)(5)(A)); must have capabilities 'to block, freeze, and reject specific or impermissible transactions'; must have 'the technological capability to comply, and will comply, with the terms of any lawful order' (§4(a)(6)(B)); 'lawful order' defined to include orders to 'seize, freeze, burn, or prevent the transfer of payment stablecoins' (§2(16)(A))
GENIUS Act is P.L. 119-27, signed 18 Jul 2025; regulators and FinCEN to write implementing rules
Tether (Feb 2026) said it had frozen about $4.2bn linked to illicit activity and worked with 310+ agencies in 64 countries incl. DOJ and Secret Service
23 Apr 2026: Tether froze >$344m USDT on two Tron addresses working with OFAC and US law enforcement; Ardoino: 'USDT is not a safe haven for illicit activity'

entries.topic: Counterweights: Signal, Carpenter, Chatrie, BIPA, Clearview 2022, MHMDA, DROP, Montana SB 282, Maven, Flock pause, UK-Apple

claims.text: In response to a C.D. Cal. grand jury subpoena seeking extensive data, Signal produced only account-creation and last-connection timestamps; 'Signal still knows nothing about you'

Carpenter (2018), 5-4, Roberts: acquiring historical cell-site location records is a search, warrant generally required; 'We decline to grant the state unrestricted access to a wireless carrier's database of physical location information'

Chatrie (29 Jun 2026): Kagan for five, Gorsuch concurring in judgment, Alito/Thomas/Barrett dissenting; accessing Location History is a search; third-party doctrine rejected; warrant validity remanded to 4th Cir.; exclusionary rule not decided

BIPA requires a written release before a private entity collects biometrics; liquidated damages $1,000 negligent / $5,000 intentional or reckless; 'A private entity does not include a State or local government agency'; Act does not apply to contractors of a State agency
Rosenbach (Ill. 2019) triggered a surge of BIPA suits; Facebook settled the Patel 'tag suggestions' case for $650 million after a $550m deal was rejected

ACLU v. Clearview consent order (11 May 2022): Clearview permanently barred from making its faceprint database available to most private entities nationwide; five-year bar on any Illinois entity incl. state and local police
Washington My Health My Data Act passed Apr 2023, effective Mar 2024, private right of action; first suit 10 Feb 2025 against Amazon over an ad SDK collecting location and ad IDs
California DROP: one deletion request to 500+ registered brokers from 1 Jan 2026; brokers process from 1 Aug 2026 every 45 days
Montana SB 282 (signed May 2025): governmental entities may not purchase communications, precise geolocation or sensitive data without a warrant or investigative subpoena; first state to do so
Google (Diane Greene, 1 Jun 2018) said Project Maven contract would not be renewed in 2019 after thousands of employees petitioned and dozens quit

Flock paused CBP and HSI pilots on 25 Aug 2025 after Illinois Secretary of State's audit found CBP accessed Illinois plate data in 'a clear violation of the state law'; CEO: 'We clearly communicated poorly'
DNI Gabbard said on 19 Aug 2025 that the UK agreed to drop its demand for a backdoor into Apple's encrypted iCloud data; Apple had stopped offering Advanced Data Protection to new UK users
